# RTX’s Pratt & Whitney initiates construction of new $100 million Rzeszów expansion to strengthen advanced manufacturing capabilities


October 23, 2026


- Share this article on Facebook
- Share this article on Twitter
- Share this article on LinkedIn
- Share this article via email


***New 6500 square-meters (70K square-foot) facility will support growing demand for commercial and military engines***


RZESZÓW, Poland (Oct. 23, 2026) – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, today announced the start of construction on a new $100 million (375 million zloty) facility to increase production capacity, introduce manufacturing of critical rotating components and meet the growing global demand for commercial and military engines, including the Pratt & Whitney GTF™, F135 and F100 engines. The expanded site is expected to become operational in 2028, creating more than 120 jobs.


The Rzeszów site provides advanced manufacturing and technology development capabilities for commercial and military engines, turboprops and auxiliary power units. Its work includes the producing critical engine components such as the GTF fan drive gear system, F100 static structures and key F135 parts. The site also manufactures engines for helicopters, business jets and general aviation aircraft — specifically those from the PT6, PW200, PW500/600 and PW800 families.


Ceremonial groundbreaking for the expansion of Pratt & Whitney’s new facility in Rzeszow, Poland. Pictured from left to right: President of Rzeszów, Konrad Fijołek; Marshal of the Podkarpacie Region, Władysław Ortyl; Governor of the Podkarpacie region, Teresa Kubas-Hul; VP & GM, Rotor Core Value Stream (RCVS) Pratt & Whitney Columbus, Jason Kosmas; General Manager of Pratt & Whitney in Rzeszów, Piotr Owsicki and entire investment team.


“Six months ago, we were talking about this investment as a plan and an opportunity to strengthen Poland’s position as a strategic center of excellence for Pratt & Whitney,” said Piotr Owsicki, general manager, Pratt & Whitney in Rzeszów. “Today, we begin turning that plan into reality. Through strong collaboration across our teams and our shared commitment to delivering for our customers, we are breaking ground on a new Rzeszów facility that will expand our ability to develop highly advanced capabilities and technologies.”


The[expansion follows and supports](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/04/22/rtxs-pratt-whitney-invests-100-million-to-increase-production-capacity-add-a) a[$200 million investment](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/02/24/rtxs-pratt-whitney-broadens-manufacturing-capabilities-with-200-million-inves) announced in February for a seventh isothermal forging press at Pratt & Whitney's Columbus Forge facility in Georgia, United States. These capital projects, expected to be fully operational by 2028, will enable a 30% increase in output of critical engine parts, such as rotating compressors and turbine disks.


Poland represents RTX's largest investment and employee base outside the United States, with more than 9,500 employees across its Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon businesses in-country.


**About Pratt & Whitney** Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities.


**About RTX** With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defence systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
